propositions.text: The Claimant, a Sri Lankan citizen, seeks refugee protection under sections 96 and 97(1) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX (the Claimant), a citizen of Sri Lanka, seeks refugee protection pursuant to sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).1

paragraphs.summary: The Claimant, a Sri Lankan citizen, seeks refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).

propositions.text: The Claimant alleges persecution in Sri Lanka due to his Tamil race.
propositions.quote: he alleges persecution in Sri Lanka as a result of his Tamil race.

paragraphs.summary: The Claimant alleges persecution in Sri Lanka due to his Tamil race.

propositions.text: The Claimant has established his identity on a balance of probabilities based on various identity documents.
propositions.quote: I find that the Claimant has established his identity on a balance of probabilities based on the copy of his Sri Lankan passport on file... and based on the following original identity documents presented at the hearing...

paragraphs.summary: The Claimant has established his identity on a balance of probabilities based on various identity documents.

propositions.text: The Claimant has not established a serious possibility of persecution due to Tamil race because his evidence is not credible.
propositions.quote: I find that the Claimant has not established that he faces a serious possibility of persecution in Sri Lanka as a result of his Tamil race because the evidence he presented that he will face this persecution is not credible.

propositions.text: The Claimant has not established on a balance of probabilities that he faces danger of torture, risk to life, or cruel and unusual treatment if returned to Sri Lanka.
propositions.quote: I also find that the Claimant has not established, on a balance of probabilities, that he would be subject to a danger of torture, or a risk to his life, or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment should he return to Sri Lanka because he has failed to present sufficient credible evidence to establish that he will face harm under section 97(1).

paragraphs.summary: The Claimant has not credibly established risk of persecution or harm if returned to Sri Lanka.

propositions.text: The determinative issue is credibility, including delay and reavailment as it relates to credibility.
propositions.quote: The determinative issue in this case is credibility, and delay and reavailment as it relates to credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The determinative issue is credibility, including delay and reavailment as it relates to credibility.

propositions.text: The Claimant testified inconsistently about how he came to police attention and gave ambiguous answers, leading to a negative credibility inference.
propositions.quote: The Claimant testified inconsistently about how he initially came to the attention of the police... I draw a negative credibility inference regarding his allegation that he was persecuted in Sri Lanka.

paragraphs.summary: The Claimant's inconsistent testimony about police attention leads to a negative credibility inference.

propositions.text: The Claimant alleges he first came to police attention in 2013 for helping relatives resettle in Colombo, involving a man named XXXX.
propositions.quote: He alleged that he first came to the attention of the police in 2013 because he helped relatives from the North resettle in Colombo... because of a man named "XXXX".

propositions.text: The Claimant was arrested and detained for three days in 2013, beaten and accused of LTTE membership.
propositions.quote: The Claimant was then arrested and detained for three days. He alleges that during his detention, he was beaten and accused of being a member of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).

paragraphs.summary: The Claimant alleges police attention in 2013 due to helping relatives and was arrested, beaten, and accused of LTTE membership.

propositions.text: Basis of Claim states the Claimant helped XXXX move from Jaffna to Colombo due to danger in Jaffna.
propositions.quote: Most of my father's relatives have been [sic] living in the northern part of Sri Lanka... He asked me to help him find accommodation... since living in Jaffna was dangerous. I found a house for them in Kotahena [Colombo]. I also helped them move in.

paragraphs.summary: Basis of Claim states the Claimant helped XXXX move from Jaffna to Colombo due to danger in Jaffna.

propositions.text: At hearing, Claimant said he helped XXXX move within Colombo, not from Jaffna to Colombo.
propositions.quote: At the hearing, the Claimant stated that he did not help XXXX move from Jaffna to Colombo. Instead, he stated that he helped XXXX move within Colombo...

propositions.text: Claimant failed to reasonably explain inconsistency about XXXX's residence and movement, negatively impacting credibility.
propositions.quote: When asked about this inconsistency, the Claimant failed to provide a reasonable explanation and instead provided roundabout answers...

paragraphs.summary: Claimant inconsistently testified about helping XXXX move, failing to explain, harming credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant's inconsistent testimony about helping XXXX negatively impacts credibility of persecution allegation.
propositions.quote: I find that the Claimant failed to testify consistently about how he helped XXXX, and his failure to provide a reasonable explanation for this inconsistency negatively impacts the credibility of his allegation that he was persecuted in Sri Lanka.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's inconsistent testimony about helping XXXX harms credibility of persecution claim.

propositions.text: Claimant's I-589 application presents a third version: he helped a relative of XXXX find housing in Colombo.
propositions.quote: In his I-589, the Claimant stated that he helped one of XXXX's relatives to find housing in Colombo...

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's I-589 application gives a third version of helping XXXX's relative find housing in Colombo.

propositions.text: Omission of XXXX's last name in Basis of Claim is significant and detracts from Claimant's credibility.
propositions.quote: I find that this is a significant omission that detracts from the credibility of the Claimant.

propositions.text: Claimant had counsel and was advised to include names, dates, places; lack of explanation for omission further detracts credibility.
propositions.quote: The Basis of Claim form clearly states that the Claimant should include dates, names and places wherever possible... Claimant's lack of reasonable explanation for why he omitted XXXX's last name detracts from the credibility...

paragraphs.summary: Omission of XXXX's last name and lack of explanation detract from Claimant's credibility.

propositions.text: At hearing, Claimant testified XXXX's last name was XXXX but gave ambiguous, convoluted reasons for omission.
propositions.quote: At the hearing, the Claimant testified that XXXX's last name was XXXX... Claimant's responses were, once again, ambiguous and convoluted.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant gave ambiguous reasons for omitting XXXX's last name at hearing.

propositions.text: Claimant's explanation for omitting XXXX's last name is unreasonable and undermines credibility.
propositions.quote: I find it unreasonable that the Claimant was not able to state clearly why he omitted XXXX's last name... The fact that XXXX was the source of the Claimant's problems is the very reason that his full name should have been included...

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's unreasonable explanation for omitting XXXX's last name undermines credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant testified inconsistently about fear of persecution after second arrest in June 2013.
propositions.quote: The Claimant testified inconsistently about his fear of persecution after his alleged second arrest in June 2013...

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified inconsistently about fear of persecution after second arrest in June 2013.

propositions.text: Claimant's ambiguous answers about fear after second arrest undermine credibility of persecution allegation.
propositions.quote: I find that the Claimant's ambiguous and roundabout answers... undermine the credibility of his allegation that he fears persecution in Sri Lanka.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's ambiguous answers about fear after second arrest undermine credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges arrest at 'shipping ministry' or 'shipping centre' while looking for a job in 2014.
propositions.quote: The Claimant alleges that he was arrested at either the "shipping ministry"... or in the "shipping centre"... to look for a job.

propositions.text: Claimant testified police came, asked his name, and took him in a Jeep without knowing how police knew he was there.
propositions.quote: The Claimant stated that while he was at the shipping centre on XXXX XXXX, 2014, four police came in, asked his name and then asked him to get in a Jeep. The Claimant stated that he did not know how the police knew he was there at the time.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant alleges 2014 arrest at shipping centre while job seeking; police took him without known reason.

propositions.text: Claimant's account of 2014 arrest is implausible; no reasonable explanation for police knowledge or timing.
propositions.quote: I find this account of his arrest implausible. I find that there is no reasonable way for the police to know that the Claimant was at the shipping centre at the time that he was.

propositions.text: This implausible account negatively impacts credibility of persecution allegation.
propositions.quote: I find that this account of his third arrest negatively impacts the credibility of his allegation that he was persecuted in Sri Lanka.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's implausible 2014 arrest account negatively impacts credibility of persecution claim.

propositions.text: Claimant decided to leave Sri Lanka in 2014 due to persecution but returned in June 2015 after six months on a boat.
propositions.quote: The Claimant testified that he decided to leave Sri Lanka because of his persecution in 2014... However, he returned to Sri Lanka in June 2015 after six months of working on a boat.

propositions.text: Claimant had valid US visa since 2010 but did not go to US in 2014, citing ship captain withholding passport.
propositions.quote: However, he had a valid visa to the United States since 2010... he did not go to the United States in 2014... because the Captain of his ship held his passport.

propositions.text: Captain withholding passport is not a reasonable explanation for delay in leaving Sri Lanka in 2014.
propositions.quote: The fact that his Captain withheld is passport is beside the point. I do not find that this is a reasonable explanation for his delay.

propositions.text: In 2015, Claimant found an agent to get passage to US; no evidence why he couldn't find one in 2014.
propositions.quote: In 2015, the Claimant stated that he found an agent to get him passage to the United States. There was no evidence presented as to why he could not have found an agent in 2014 to help him leave Sri Lanka.

propositions.text: Claimant's reavailment to Sri Lanka inconsistent with genuine fear of persecution and undermines credibility.
propositions.quote: I find that the Claimant's reavailment inconsistent with a genuine fear of persecution in Sri Lanka and that it undermines the credibility of his allegation that he was being persecuted.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's delay and return to Sri Lanka despite US visa undermines credibility of persecution fear.

propositions.text: Claimant gave inconsistent reasons for returning to Sri Lanka in 2014 and living illegally in US in 2015.
propositions.quote: The Claimant also gave inconsistent testimony... He stated that he did not want to live anywhere illegally. However, in 2015 he went to live in the United States illegally.

propositions.text: This inconsistency further undermines credibility of genuine fear of persecution in Sri Lanka.
propositions.quote: I find that this further undermines the credibility of his allegation that he has a genuine fear of persecution in Sri Lanka.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's inconsistent testimony about illegal residence further undermines credibility of persecution fear.

propositions.text: Claimant's delay in claiming refugee status in the US undermines credibility of his fear of persecution in Sri Lanka
propositions.quote: I find that the Claimant's delay in claiming refugee status in the United States undermines the credibility of his allegation that he fears persecution in Sri Lanka.

propositions.text: Claimant planned to leave Sri Lanka due to fear of persecution
propositions.quote: The Claimant stated that he made plans to leave Sri Lanka because of his fear of persecution.

propositions.text: Claimant arrived in US early 2015 and met friend who told him about refugee system same month
propositions.quote: The Claimant arrived in the United States in early XXXX 2015. He met the friend who told him about the refugee system the same month.

propositions.text: Claimant only signed asylum application end of March 2016
propositions.quote: However, the Claimant only signed his application for asylum at the end of March 2016.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant's delay in claiming refugee status in the US undermines his fear of persecution claim, noting his arrival and application dates.

propositions.text: Delay inconsistent with genuine fear of persecution
propositions.quote: I find this delay inconsistent with a genuine fear of persecution in Sri Lanka.

propositions.text: Claimant intended not to return to Sri Lanka
propositions.quote: The Claimant alleged that he had an intention not to return to Sri Lanka.

propositions.text: By not claiming refugee status, claimant risked deportation to Sri Lanka
propositions.quote: By failing to claim refugee status, the Claimant chose to risk being deported back to Sri Lanka.

propositions.text: Delay undermines claimant's subjective fear of returning to Sri Lanka
propositions.quote: I find that the Claimant's delay in the United States in claiming refugee status is inconsistent with a subjective fear of returning to Sri Lanka and that it undermines his allegation that he fears persecution in Sri Lanka.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant's delay inconsistent with genuine fear and undermining his subjective fear of persecution in Sri Lanka.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges he will be stopped and jailed or questioned if returning to Sri Lanka
propositions.quote: The Claimant alleges that if he returns to Sri Lanka, he will be stopped at or right outside the airport and put in jail or asked questions.

propositions.text: Claimant presented no evidence supporting belief he would be stopped or jailed
propositions.quote: However, he presented no evidence of why he believed this might be the case.

propositions.text: Claimant testified police searched for him once after first arrest in 2013 or 2014, testimony inconsistent
propositions.quote: To the contrary, the Claimant testified that the police have only come to search for him once, either after his first arrest in March 2013 or in 2014 (his testimony on this issue was inconsistent).

propositions.text: No evidence claimant wanted by police since 2014; he is not wanted if he returns
propositions.quote: As there is no evidence that the Claimant has been wanted by the police since 2014, I find that he is not wanted by the police should he return to Sri Lanka.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges risk of detention if returned, but court finds no evidence and no police interest since 2014.

propositions.text: Having found claimant not credible on past persecution, must consider risk of persecution based on profile
propositions.quote: Having found that the Claimant is not credible regarding his past persecution, I must now consider whether the Claimant will face a serious possibility of persecution should he return to Sri Lanka because of his profile as a young Tamil male who has been living abroad and is returning as a failed refugee claimant.

paragraphs.summary: Court proceeds to consider risk of persecution based on claimant's profile after finding past persecution claim not credible.

propositions.text: Claimant does not have well-founded fear of persecution based on profile as young Tamil male returning as failed refugee
propositions.quote: I find that the Claimant does not have a well-founded fear of persecution simply on the basis of his profile as a young Tamil male who has been living abroad and is returning as a failed refugee claimant.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds claimant lacks well-founded fear of persecution based on his profile as a young Tamil male returning as failed refugee.

propositions.text: Evidence on treatment of returning Tamils is mixed
propositions.quote: The evidence in the National Documentation Package on Sri Lanka is mixed regarding the treatment of returning Tamils.

propositions.text: Most reliable evidence is from UNHCR, an international refugee support organization
propositions.quote: I find that the most reliable evidence on the subject comes from the United Nations High Commission on Refugees (UNHCR) because it is an international organization responsible for supporting and protecting refugees.

propositions.text: UNHCR assists Sri Lankan and Indian governments in resettling Tamil refugees and monitors reintegration
propositions.quote: The UNHCR has also been assisting the Sri Lankan and Indian governments in a program to resettle Tamil refugees in Sri Lanka as well as monitoring their resettlement in Sri Lanka and conducting studies on the reintegration of Tamils into Sri Lanka.

propositions.text: UNHCR evidence more reliable than claimant's country condition articles for same reasons
propositions.quote: I find that this evidence is also more reliable than the country conditions articles filed by the Claimant for the same reasons.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds UNHCR evidence on returning Tamils most reliable and more credible than claimant's country condition articles.

propositions.text: UNHCR Guidelines limit risk profile to those with links beyond residency in LTTE-controlled areas
propositions.quote: The UNHCR Guidelines indicate that the risk profile for people with suspected links to the LTTE does not include every Tamil or even every individual who may be suspected of links to the LTTE.

propositions.text: LTTE controlled 76% of northern and eastern Sri Lanka in 2000-2001
propositions.quote: At the height of its influence in Sri Lanka in 2000-2001, the LTTE controlled and administered 76% of what are now the northern and eastern provinces of Sri Lanka.

propositions.text: Living in LTTE-controlled area alone does not create refugee protection need
propositions.quote: Originating from an area that was previously controlled by the LTTE does not in itself result in a need for international refugee protection in the sense of the 1951 Convention and its 1967 Protocol.

propositions.text: Links beyond residency expose individuals to treatment possibly requiring refugee protection depending on case specifics
propositions.quote: However, previous (real or perceived) links that go beyond prior residency within an area controlled by the LTTE continue to expose individuals to treatment which may give rise to a need for international refugee protection, depending on the specifics of the individual case.

propositions.text: More elaborate links include senior LTTE positions, former combatants, supporters, fundraisers, and close family
propositions.quote: The nature of these more elaborate links to the LTTE can vary, but may include people with the following profiles: 1) Persons who held senior positions with considerable authority in the LTTE civilian administration... 6) Persons with family links or who are dependent on or otherwise closely related to the persons with the above profiles.

paragraphs.summary: Court explains UNHCR guidelines limiting refugee risk to those with links beyond residency in LTTE areas, listing relevant profiles.

propositions.text: Being a young Tamil male alone does not expose one to serious persecution in Sri Lanka
propositions.quote: I find that based on this evidence, merely being a young Tamil male does not expose one to a serious possibility of persecution in Sri Lanka.

propositions.text: Persecution requires active/formal LTTE involvement or close relation to such persons
propositions.quote: Rather, in order to be subject to persecution, one has to have been actively and formally involved in the LTTE, or a close relation of those actively and formally involved in the LTTE.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges no links to LTTE
propositions.quote: The Claimant alleged that he had no such links to the LTTE.

propositions.text: Claimant does not face serious persecution risk simply as young Tamil male returning as failed refugee
propositions.quote: As a result, I find that he does not face a serious possibility of persecution simply because he is a young Tamil male returning as a failed refugee.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds claimant's lack of LTTE links means he faces no serious persecution risk as a young Tamil male returning failed refugee.

propositions.text: Claimant has not established serious possibility of persecution based on profile as young Tamil male returning failed refugee
propositions.quote: I find that the Claimant has not established that he will face a serious possibility of persecution simply on the basis that he is a young Tamil male returning as a failed refugee claimant.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds claimant failed to establish serious persecution risk based on his profile as young Tamil male returning failed refugee.

propositions.text: Claimant failed to provide credible evidence of serious possibility of persecution
propositions.quote: As the Claimant has failed to provide sufficient credible evidence to establish that he faces a serious possibility of persecution,

propositions.text: Claimant failed to meet higher threshold to be person in need of protection
propositions.quote: I find that he has also failed to present sufficient credible evidence to meet the higher threshold test to establish that he is a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds claimant failed to provide credible evidence of persecution or meet threshold as person in need of protection.

propositions.text: Claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection
propositions.quote: Having considered all the evidence, I find that the Claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection and rejects claim.
